correlation_score — REPRCONV score op

• Data kinds: voxel × voxel → score

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.correlation_score(voxel_a, voxel_b) (to call the implementation directly, import reprconv; reprconv.correlation_score(voxel_a, voxel_b); from the registry, opsreprconv.get("correlation_score"))

Usage

Two voxel → a normalised cross-correlation score volume. The only entry into this type.

score is a type that refine_peak_newton consumes, but no op in the ledger produced score (measured; it was reached only after a generator seed was planted). Here it returns the circular cross-correlation via FFT:

score[s] = sum_x (a[x] - mean_a) * (b[x + s] - mean_b) / (N * std_a * std_b)

So if b is a shifted by s0 with np.roll, the peak stands exactly at s0 (closed-form ground truth; the test uses this). Being a circular correlation, the edges wrap around -- it is stated explicitly that this is not a truncated correlation.

Args:

voxel_a: (D, H, W).

voxel_b: (D, H, W), same shape as voxel_a.

Returns:

(D, H, W) float64, range roughly [-1, 1] (1.0 for a perfect match).

Raises:

ValueError: not 3-D / shapes differ / constant volume (standard deviation 0) / non-finite.
